ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 289, 292 and 254 (company name and stock corporation formation); Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 10456, as amended), Articles 2, 5 and 8; Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 10696, as amended), Article 4 and Enforcement Decree, applying customer due diligence and beneficial-owner identification at the 25% threshold; Real Name Financial Transactions Act (Act No. 3602, as amended); Regulation on the Identification of Customers and Beneficial Owners under the Financial Services Commission and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) rules, as supplemented by FATF Recommendations 10, 12 and 24.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of each foreign corporate shareholder/UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or corporate registrar in the UBO's jurisdiction of incorporation; if the UBO is Korean, the relevant District Court Registry under the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel paths only: (A) Hague Apostille Convention state: Apostille by the competent authority in the country of issuance and then submission to Korea; (B) Non-Contracting state: authentication by the local competent authority and then consular legalization by the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of Korea with territorial jurisdiction. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of each foreign corporate shareholder/UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar or government authority in the UBO's jurisdiction of incorporation, or the District Tax Office in Korea for a Korean resident corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel paths only: (A) Hague Apostille Convention state: apostille by the issuing state's competent apostille authority; (B) Non-Contracting state: local authentication followed by consular legalization at the Korean embassy or consulate with jurisdiction. The two authentication systems are alternative and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney of the corporate shareholder/UBO authorizing the incorporation of the Korean Chusik Hoesa and appointment of its resident directors and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or equivalent governing body of the corporate shareholder/UBO, with notarization by a notary public in the jurisdiction where the resolution is executed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel paths only: (A) Hague member state: apostille by the state where the notary is commissioned and the board resolution is executed; (B) Non-member state: notarization, then local foreign ministry authentication, then consular legalization by the Korean embassy or consulate with jurisdiction. Apostille and consular legalization are never cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (charter) of the corporate shareholder/UBO and approved draft Korean Articles of Incorporation for the Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or notary in the UBO's jurisdiction for the shareholder's charter; Korean notary public for the draft Korean Articles of Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For the UBO charter: parallel Hague apostille or consular legalization, as applicable. For the Korean Articles of Incorporation: notarization by a Korean notary and submission to the Korean District Court Registry; no foreign apostille or consular legalization is required for the domestic Korean charter. Do not combine foreign and Korean authentication paths for the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter, account history, and source of funds confirmation for the corporate shareholder/UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank holding the shareholder/UBO's operational account, with CDD records and authorized signatory attestation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel paths only: (A) Apostille member state: bank letter notarized and then apostilled by the competent authority of the bank's country; (B) Non-member state: bank letter notarized, authenticated by the local foreign ministry, and then consular legalized by the Korean embassy or consulate with jurisdiction. The two authentication methods must never be applied sequentially to the same certificate.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Registration Matters of the Korean Chusik Hoesa (official registry extract issued post-incorporation, required for bank account opening completion)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registry of the registered-head-office district within the Supreme Court of Korea structure
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Korean registry certificate: issued directly by the District Court Registry; when used in Korea no apostille is needed. If it must be used abroad, only the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille path applies for Hague member states; for non-member states use MOFA legalization plus destination-country consular legalization. Never chain the two paths.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, 5% or greater shareholders, directors, and authorized representatives must be screened continuously against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, the EU Consolidated List, the Korean KoFIU designation list, FATF public statements, domestic Korean law-enforcement sanctions lists, and adverse-media databases. Automated real-time screening must be completed before incorporation and refreshed at least quarterly. For any politically exposed person, whether domestic, foreign, or international, the compliance officer must obtain written senior-management approval, verify source of wealth and source of funds, apply enhanced ongoing monitoring, and report any unusual transaction to KoFIU without delay.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office Internet Registration Office (IRO) through the National Court Information Center trade-name and company-name clearance portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory trade name for a Korean stock corporation must be registered in Korean script and include the corporate-form suffix 'Jusik Hoesa' (also historically transliterated as 'Chusik Hoesa'). A parallel English name may be used contractually but cannot replace the registered Korean legal name. The official romanization follows the Revised Romanization of Korean; the exact Korean script remains decisive for registration and banking records. Name clearance applies a four-tier convention: (1) corporate form suffix 'Jusik Hoesa'; (2) distinctive core name element; (3) business-object descriptor such as 'Data Center' or 'Server Leasing'; and (4) optional English parallel transliteration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: After a name rejection, the registry office will issue a written refusal stating the conflicting registered name and the statutory ground. The applicant may immediately file a revised trade name while the incorporation file remains open; if the original clearance window is consumed, a fresh reservation must be submitted before the 30-day period expires. If the registrar still refuses, the applicant must file a written objection with the district court within two weeks under Article 104 of the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act, attaching the proposed name, search evidence, and legal argument that the name is neither identical nor misleadingly similar to any prior registration. Korean counsel should attend the hearing and, for foreign-invested companies, request expedited administrative coordination through the Foreign Investment Promotion Act mechanism. The rejection order is subject to formal judicial appeal only after the two-week objection is exhausted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The Commercial Act requires the Korean Chusik Hoesa to state a registered head office (dae-pyo-jeom) in Korea, but it does not mandate the ownership of physical premises at the moment of incorporation. However, for a data-center colocation and bare-metal server leasing business under ISIC 6209, the National Tax Service and commercial banks reject a purely postal mailbox or agency-only virtual office. In practice, tax authorities treat a registered office as the business place for VAT, corporate tax filing, and invoice issuance; a virtual office is accepted only if there is a real administrative presence, a permanent signboard, staff, the actual lease is in the company's name, and mail can be physically received. Leading Korean banks and KoFIU-CDD procedures require the business address to match the registered address and demand a lease agreement and utility bill in the company's name. Recommendation: rent serviced office space for at least six months and maintain an onsite local administrator for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspection risk is moderate; quantified probability is approximately 35-50% within the first 12 months for a newly VAT-registered entity in the ICT leasing sector. Inspection checklist: (1) registered company signboard physically displayed; (2) lease agreement in the company's name and matching registration; (3) utility bills, electricity and telecom invoices; (4) local employment records and payroll evidence; (5) colocation rack-server or bare-metal leasing master agreements; (6) network and bandwidth invoices; (7) internal AML/CFT policy and customer files; and (8) sample books and records. Municipal license officers and National Tax Service field staff may perform unannounced inspections under the Local Tax Act and VAT procedures; advance notice is not required.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act (상법), Articles 288-317 (incorporation of stock corporations), Article 289 (Articles of Incorporation), Article 290 (registration of incorporation), Article 292 (capital), Article 295 (subscription of shares), Article 302 (first board meeting), Article 317 (registration of incorporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registry Office (등기소) under the Supreme Court of Korea, specifically the local district court registry with jurisdiction over the registered office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (정관) and Application for Registration of Incorporation (설립등록신청서)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement under Korean law. Capital may be set at any amount, including 1 KRW. No blocked escrow account requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (the 'Company'), a Chusik Hoesa (Stock Corporation) incorporated under the laws of the Republic of Korea.

The undersigned, being the duly appointed directors of the Company, hereby convene and hold the first meeting of the Board of Directors on this [date] day of [month], [year], at [time] at the registered office of the Company. The meeting is called with due notice and in accordance with Article 6 of the Korean Commercial Act. All directors are present, and the meeting is validly constituted.

After due deliberation, the following resolutions are unanimously passed:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The Board acknowledges that the initial share capital of the Company is [amount] KRW, divided into [number] shares of no par value. The Board confirms that all shares have been fully subscribed and paid in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation and the Korean Commercial Act. The Board authorizes the issuance of share certificates to the subscribers and the recording of such subscriptions in the Company's register of shareholders.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby authorizes the opening of corporate bank accounts with [Bank Name] and appoints the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer as authorized signatories. The Board authorizes the execution of all banking documents, the establishment of electronic banking protocols, and the use of the Company's corporate seal for banking purposes. The Board further authorizes the appointment of any additional signatories as may be required by the bank.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board adopts the registered office of the Company at [address], Republic of Korea, as the principal place of business and legal seat of the Company. The Board authorizes the registration of such address with the competent Court Registry and the National Tax Service, and the execution of any lease or service agreements necessary for the maintenance of such office.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board appoints [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Auditor (if applicable) for the term as provided in the Articles of Incorporation. The Board authorizes the execution of all documents and filings required to effectuate these appointments, including the filing of the directors' and auditor's consents with the Court Registry.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes any director or officer to take all necessary actions, execute all contracts, and make all filings required to comply with these resolutions, including but not limited to filings with the Court Registry, the National Tax Service, and any other governmental authority. This authorization includes the power to engage legal counsel and other professional advisors as needed.

This resolution is effective immediately and shall be recorded in the minutes of this meeting.

[Signature of Directors]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (공증사) and local Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, including the company name, business purpose, registered office address, authorized share capital, number of shares, and details of initial directors and auditor. The incorporators must sign the document, and it must be notarized by a licensed notary public. After notarization, the document becomes the foundational charter of the company. Ensure all statutory requirements under Articles 289-292 of the Korean Commercial Act are met. Submit the notarized Articles to the Court Registry for preliminary review if required.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney (if any incorporator is represented)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or Court Registry identifies deficiencies, correct the Articles and resubmit. Common issues include incomplete business purpose clauses or missing signatures. Legal counsel can assist in rectifying the document within 2 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Capital and Obtain Certificate of Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Bank (e.g., Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank) or any licensed financial institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate bank account in the name of the company (pre-incorporation account) and deposit the full amount of the subscribed capital. The bank will issue a certificate of capital deposit (자본금 납입증명서) confirming the deposit. This certificate is a mandatory document for the incorporation registration. The deposit must be made by the subscribers or their authorized representatives, and the account must be in the exact name of the company as stated in the Articles.
required_dossiers: Identification of the person making the deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening due to incomplete documentation, provide the missing documents and reapply. If the deposit is not made in full, the certificate will not be issued; ensure the exact capital amount is transferred.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Registration with Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registry (등기소) with jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation (설립등록신청서) to the Court Registry, along with the notarized Articles, certificate of capital deposit, and other required documents. The application must include the company name, registered office, capital, shares, and details of directors and auditor. The Court will review the application and, if satisfied, issue a Certificate of Incorporation (법인등기부등본). The registration fee must be paid at the time of filing.
required_dossiers: Consent forms from directors and auditor (if any)
Power of attorney (if filed by agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Court Registry issues a query or suspension, review the notice and correct any deficiencies (e.g., missing signatures, incorrect capital amount). Resubmit the corrected application within 10 days. If the issue is substantive, seek legal advice to amend the Articles or other documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with National Tax Service for Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (국세청) or local tax office (세무서)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Certificate of Incorporation, file for business registration (사업자등록) with the local tax office. Submit the incorporation certificate, lease agreement for the registered office, and identification of the representative. The tax office will issue a Business Registration Certificate (사업자등록증) which is required for tax invoicing and banking. This step must be completed within 20 days of incorporation to avoid penalties.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of office address
Identification of the CEO and other officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests additional information, provide the requested documents within 5 business days. If the lease agreement is insufficient, provide a certificate of address or a notarized consent from the property owner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Court Registry, National Tax Service, and local municipal authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporate seal (법인인감) with the Court Registry to obtain a seal certificate (인감증명서). Activate the corporate bank account by submitting the incorporation certificate and seal certificate. Additionally, register for social insurance (National Pension, Health Insurance, Employment Insurance) with the relevant authorities. Ensure all statutory filings are made within the prescribed deadlines.
required_dossiers: Corporate seal and seal registration application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If seal registration is delayed, expedite by providing all required documents. For social insurance, if registration is missed, file for retroactive registration with penalties. Engage a local compliance advisor to ensure all post-incorporation obligations are met.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity that commences a Korean taxable business, including data-center colocation leasing in Korea, must obtain a Korean Business Registration Certificate (BRC), which is the combined TIN/VAT ID. Step 1: Determine the Korean VAT taxable establishment or fixed local place of business; a lease agreement for the Korean data-center facility should be in place. Step 2: Appoint a Korean tax representative if the foreign entity has no habitual domicile or local physical establishment, as required by the Framework Act on National Taxes. Step 3: Prepare the foreign entity's certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, board resolution authorizing the Korean operation, passport of the authorized representative, power of attorney, and proof of the local Korean business address. Step 4: File Form for Business Registration (Business Operator Registration) with the NTS through the HomeTax portal using the foreign-business registration channel, or in person with the district tax office that has jurisdiction over the Korean place of business. Step 5: receive the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which is used for corporate income tax, VAT withholding, e-tax invoice issuance, and customs-related indirect tax purposes. The Korean TIN and VAT ID are the same number; no separate VAT ID is issued.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None equivalent to a check-the-box election under Korean law. A Chusik Hoesa is automatically classified as a domestic corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax and VAT. Statutory elective mechanisms are limited to Korean consolidated corporate tax filing for 100% domestic subsidiaries and voluntary VAT registration for non-resident suppliers before the first taxable supply. No hybrid mismatch election or fiscal-transparent entity election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None - VAT registration is mandatory from the moment a taxable business commences in Korea, regardless of turnover. There is no turnover threshold postponing registration for corporations. For foreign non-resident suppliers, registration is required before the first taxable supply unless a reverse-charge or direct import mechanism applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All taxable business persons in Korea must issue VAT invoices for taxable supplies, and corporations are required to issue electronic tax invoices (e-tax invoices; e-segye-gyesanseo) through HomeTax or a certified AGT (ASP) integrator. For B2B supplies, the e-tax invoice must be transmitted to the NTS by the day following the tax invoice issuance date. There is no separate real-time cryptographic clearance or anti-fraud stamping regime; however, the NTS performs near-real-time data matching, cross-referencing e-tax invoice filings, cash receipts, and VAT returns, and mandates API/Hometax electronic transmission for automated filing. Failure to issue and report electronic tax invoices triggers penalty surcharges.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export VAT treatment is available under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act Article 21 for (i) exported goods where the goods are physically removed from Korea and the export declaration is accepted by Korea Customs Service; and (ii) qualifying exported/foreign-earning services supplied to non-residents, including services that are actually consumed outside Korea, international transport services, and services directly related to export trade. For data-center colocation leasing of rack space, power, cooling, and bare-metal hosting located in Korea, the place of supply is deemed to be Korea and the standard 10% VAT rate applies. The service is not eligible for zero-rating merely because the customer is a foreign resident. Only separately identifiable cross-border digital/cloud services that are supplied from Korea and actually used or consumed outside Korea could potentially qualify for zero-rating, subject to stringent documentary proof of foreign use and foreign-currency receipt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS Export Declaration Acceptance (export declaration with customs clearance confirmation)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical delivery outside Korea
Foreign exchange settlement record / inward remittance certificate issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing actual offshore payment receipt
Export/offshore service contract and, where applicable, documentary evidence that services were actually used or consumed outside Korea
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service audit zero-rated export claims by matching export declarations, electronic tax invoices, foreign exchange receipts, and corporate VAT returns. If an exporter fails to collect export consideration within 180 days or submits false or insufficient documentation, the zero-rating is retrospectively denied, and the NTS assesses output VAT at 10% on the suppressed supply. Penalty surcharges under the Framework Act on National Taxes are imposed, generally 10% of the unpaid VAT for negligent under-declaration and up to 40% for fraudulent under-declaration, in addition to daily interest on the delayed payment. Willful fraud may also trigger criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) acting through the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; the Bank of Korea administers foreign exchange oversight with the Korea Customs Service as operational monitoring agent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South Korean won is fully convertible for current account transactions under Article 3 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, including trade settlements, service fees, and profit remittances. Capital account transactions, however, are governed by a negative list system requiring prior declaration or approval from the designated foreign exchange bank when the transaction falls outside the pre-authorized categories. Korean entities receiving foreign currency export proceeds are generally mandated to convert such proceeds into won within the statutory deadline or hold them in a foreign currency account, but the latter requires justification. For a data center colocation leasing entity, cross-border monthly lease fees from overseas customers would be current account receipts (service export under ISIC 6209), which are freely convertible subject to verification of the underlying invoice. Profit remittance in the form of dividends to non-resident shareholders is legal, but requires a Foreign Exchange Bank confirmation of the entity's audited financial statements, withholding tax clearance from the National Tax Service (NTS), and a certificate of foreign investment registration if the shareholding is foreign-direct-investment based. In practice, the Bank of Korea's annual Foreign Exchange Reform Plans have progressively liberalized controls, but the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations still require the submission of a purchase/sale confirmation and a customs declaration for amounts exceeding 50,000 USD, effectively creating friction for large lump-sum data center equipment imports. Surrender requirements were substantially relaxed in 2017, but repatriation of export proceeds must be completed within a prescribed period to avoid penalties. The Ministry of Economy and Finance periodically reviews the basis for restricting speculative FX transactions, and any mass remittance pattern from the Korean entity without corresponding service contracts would raise Bank of Korea inspection flags. Realistically, for recurring colocation lease income, the main hurdle is not currency conversion itself but the requirement to establish a clear underlying services contract with accurate HS/ECC codes and an annual settlement report to the bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For exports of services under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, Korean exporters must receive their foreign currency proceeds through an authorized foreign exchange bank and, for goods exports, the proceeds must be settled within 18 months from the shipment date (recently extended to 24 months for certain SME categories); for service exports such as data center colocation, receipts are generally required to be converted into won when the counterparty is a non-resident, unless the entity operates a designated Foreign Currency Account with the bank's prior approval. The mandatory conversion ratio is effectively 0% after the 2017 deregulation, as the surrender requirement for export proceeds was eliminated, but the exporter must report the receipt via the Foreign Exchange Information System within 30 business days. If the Korean entity chooses to retain foreign currency in a domestic bank account, it must file an acquisition report and apply the proceeds for approved purposes only.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW) plus Foreign Currency Demand Deposit Account (USD/JPY/EUR)
Corporate operating account and Foreign Exchange Settlement Account with Trade Service center
Capital Escrow Account for inbound Foreign Direct Investment and operational current account
Cross-border USD collection account and treasury settlement account with dedicated FX dealing desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Non-viable for storing corporate treasury balances: South Korea does not license standalone digital EMI entities; foreign fintech EMIs such as Revolut Business, Airwallex, and Payoneer cannot provide local IBANs or operate as regulated deposit-taking institutions for KRW. They may be used peripherally as a payment collection gateway for international customers denominated in USD, but funds must ultimately be swept into a South Korean licensed bank account or a properly registered foreign exchange broker under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. Legal constraint: only banks licensed under the Korean Banking Act can open won-denominated business accounts; any remittance via an unlicensed EMI triggers Bank of Korea foreign exchange reporting and could be treated as unauthorized foreign exchange business. Therefore, the treasury blueprint mandates a domestic tier-1 bank as the primary clearing node, with EMIs relegated to a non-core ancillary invoicing tool if they hold an overseas MSB/fintech license and are used solely for receivables conversion.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person physical appearance is required for the statutory director (with an original corporate seal certificate, certified copy of the articles of incorporation, and photo ID) to execute the corporate account opening; however, for non-resident directors, South Korean banks permit a remote consular proxy opening where the director physically attends the Korean consulate/embassy or a notary public abroad to sign the signature book and POA, followed by courier submission of the notarized documents to the branch. The actual bank interview can be conducted via video call with the compliance officer, but the document legalization must be apostilled for Hague Convention jurisdictions. For high-value capital escrow accounts linked to foreign investment, the non-resident investor must submit a Foreign Exchange Declaration Certificate (FEDC) before the account is provisionally activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual ownership combination: non-resident directors holding 100% shares of a Chusik Hoesa whose business is primarily cross-border service export, while the entity id is formed as a local data center operator without any physical server facility lease contracts presented at onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized board resolution appointing the legal representative, a five-year master colocation lease agreement with a Korean data center landlord or proof of ownership/lease of the server racks, a corporate registry listing (deung-gi sahang jeungmyeongseo), plus an organizational chart showing the ultimate beneficial owner's background and source of wealth declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring high-volume inbound USD wire transfers from multiple unrelated overseas customers with same-day clustering and rapid onward transfer to third-country equipment vendors, resembling pass-through or money laundering layering due to absence of consistently matching monthly billing cycles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete invoicing and billing register, detailed service order forms for each colocation customer, monthly bandwidth/power consumption reports from the data center operator, the entity's audited financial statements for the prior two years, and a written explanation of the payment settlement cycle executed by an external CPA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failed FATCA and CRS self-certification: the Korean entity's agent fails to provide a valid W-8BEN-E, notice of U.S. trade/business presence, or a CRS Self-Certification for all controlling persons, which causes the bank to downgrade the account to a restricted debit-only profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed IRS Form W-8BEN-E with valid EIN from the U.S. Internal Revenue Service if any U.S. Pmt is made; CRS entity self-certification and individual control-person forms for all natural persons; proof of non-U.S. ownership from the corporate registry; and if applicable, a waiver from the Korean withholding tax authorities to confirm no U.S. source income.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between minimum capital requirement (zero) stated in the metadata and the Korean Commercial Act expectation of an adequate capital base for a data center operator; the bank may classify the account as high-risk due to inadequate paid-in capital (1 KRW) and debt-to-equity mismatch.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A statutory capital injection plan certified by a CPA, bank reference letters showing existing shareholders' funding capacity, shareholder loan agreements or deposit certificates, a written memorandum from the legal counsel explaining the limited liability nature of the entity under the Korean Commercial Act, and the firm's projected cash flow statement that demonstrates recurring lease revenues sufficient to cover operating costs.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound FDI capital must be declared through the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) via the receiving bank prior to remittance; use the Foreign Investment Declaration with purpose code 9211 (equity capital, non-resident direct investment). The actual capital injection is transmitted via SWIFT MT103 from the investing company's bank to the Korean bank account using the entity's account name as 'KR_CHUSIKHOESA' and a clear remittance reference of 'EQUITY INJECTION', followed by issuance of the Foreign Investment Certificate (FIC) by the bank within 4 weeks. For non-equity loans (debt financing), use purpose code 5211 with a loan agreement and interest rate schedule. After bank verification of the SWIFT crediting, the bank records the inflow on the Foreign Exchange Purchase and Sale Confirmation and the company must apply the capital only to the approved commercial scope; domestic KRW settlement to pay data center electricity and rack maintenance is executed through the KRW account without further FEIS reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Overseas trade disbursements by the Korean data center entity for equipment purchases (servers, cooling, UPS) to foreign vendors are executed through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from the Korean bank's treasury system, with the entity submitting a purchase contract, customs declaration from Korea Customs Service, and invoice to request the Foreign Exchange Bank's approval. For rolling purchase arrangements, Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C at sight or usance) can be issued through Shinhan or Kookmin for deferred settlement; Documentary Collections (D/C) are acceptable when the bank maintains the entity's cargo documents under the collection instruction, but due to the service-driven and recurring nature of data center lease revenue, the dominant clearing rail is ordinary cross-border wire via the SWIFT network. All outbound payments require the submission of a legally prescribed foreign exchange confirmation form (buyer report), and those exceeding 50,000 USD require submission of underlying transaction documents; payment to a tax-haven jurisdiction triggers enhanced review by Korea Customs Service.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forward contracts (NDFs) are generally not permissible for onshore firms unless there is a non-resident counterparty arbitrage exception; the permissible instrument is the standard onshore forward contract against USD/KRW only if real trade exposure exists under an underlying colocation lease contract.
Rolling short-term FX forward contracts with tenors under 12 months for profit remittance conversion, subject to documentary proof of receivables from non-resident clients.

Currency swaps are permissible only with licensed Korean banks and only for the purpose of converting an FCY loan asset or liability into KRW, not for speculative trading; a plain-vanilla interest rate and currency swap can be posted against the firm's USD lease receivable book.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps are allowed to hedge the foreign currency debt exposure but require Bank of Korea reporting with an executed ISDA Master Agreement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, by March 31 of the following tax year, with a permitted one-month extension only for statutorily recognized grounds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled return: additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; underreported income: additional tax of 10% of the understated tax; unpaid principal: daily delinquency charge of 0.025% plus collection via asset attachment under the National Tax Collection Act; prolonged non-filing and location evasion trigger business registration cancellation and, under Commercial Act Article 520, potential court-ordered dissolution after five years without a valid shareholders meeting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Si/Gun/Gu municipal tax authority of the registered head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, by April 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or unfiled local return: additional tax of 20% of payable local corporate income tax; underreporting: 10% surcharge on omitted tax; late payment: 0.025% per day on the amount in arrears; the municipality may enforce collection by seizure and public auction; no valid local return for consecutive years is treated as evidence of business dormancy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after fiscal year-end for calendar-year companies (April 30), provided the audited entity must first table the audited accounts at the annual shareholders meeting held within three months of fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an independent certified auditor or to file the audit report is subject to administrative fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, corrective orders by the Financial Services Commission, publication of noncompliance, and designation of an auditor by the authorities at the company's cost; persistent failure can lead to compulsory enforcement and referral for criminal penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders Meeting Records and Statutory Register Maintenance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records retained at the registered head office, subject to inspection by shareholders and verification by the National Tax Service and the district registration court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual shareholders meeting must be summoned and held within three months after the close of the fiscal year; notice to shareholders must be sent at least two weeks before the meeting date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-maintenance of the minutes and statutory registers triggers criminal administrative fines for directors under the Commercial Act; failure to hold any shareholders meeting for five years is a statutory cause for court-ordered dissolution of the Chusik Hoesa.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The sole quantitative balance-sheet trigger under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies is total assets equal to or exceeding KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.0 million) at the end of the fiscal year; listed corporations, public-interest companies, and financial or securities-licensed entities are subject to mandatory independent certified audit regardless of asset size; for a private ISIC 6209 data-center colocation lessor, turnover and headcount are not standalone statutory audit triggers but the KRW 12 billion asset condition applies cumulatively with the requirement that audited statements be filed with the FSS.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for public-interest and listed entities; privately held Chusik Hoesa may apply Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) or the Korean SME Accounting Standards while remaining compliant with the Act on External Audit and the Korean Auditing Standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Chusik Hoesa is required to keep a current shareholder register; a transferee becomes protected only after the transfer is recorded in the register. The board may set a record date and close the register for up to three months before the AGM; outside this window, every share transfer must be registered without unreasonable delay. There is no standalone annual Korean UBO government return for a non-public company, but any foreign-investor share subscription, transfer, or capital change must be reported through the foreign exchange bank and to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy within 30 days of the event, and the company must provide current benefit-owner documentation to banks under the AML framework at account refresh. The AGM annually confirms the record date and the approved shareholder list.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - 30,000 per year for a mandatory certified audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal Korean corporate income tax rate (progressive brackets: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% over KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion; 21% over KRW 20 billion up to KRW 300 billion; 24% over KRW 300 billion). A 10% local income tax surtax is imposed on assessed corporate tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory incentives include: (i) R&D tax credits of up to 30-50% of eligible R&D expenditure under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act; (ii) tax holiday and reduction for qualified foreign-invested corporations in Free Economic Zones or Foreign Investment Zones; (iii) special tax reductions for new-growth engine industry facilities; (iv) facility investment tax credits for data-center assets; (v) foreign tax credit relief under the Corporate Tax Act; used cumulatively, these can drive the effective rate materially below the 24% headline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Official return: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Return (Corporate Income Tax Return, CTA Form 1 and mandatory schedules) filed through the Korea National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing system; for Chusik Hoesa, the final return is Form 1 plus Schedule 2 (taxable income calculation), Schedule 3 (loss carryforward), Schedule 4 (tax credits), Schedule 12 (related-party international transactions), Schedule 15 (withholding on non-resident), and Schedule 16 (foreign tax credit).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final filing, with mandatory semi-annual estimated corporate tax prepayments within 3 months of the end of the first half of each fiscal year; final annual return is due within 3 months after fiscal year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final return deadline: within 3 months after the close of the fiscal year (e.g., a 31 December fiscal year-end must be filed by 31 March of the following year). Tax agents may obtain a one-month extension; foreign-invested corporations should align with the audited financial statements and statutory audit deadlines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification, corporate form, business registration number, industry classification and fiscal-year commencement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the Korean-resident Chusik Hoesa, enter ISIC 6209 / NAICS 518210 as the primary revenue industry. Disclose every non-resident shareholder in the foreign ownership schedule, including ownership percentage, country of residence, and relationship under LCITA. If any director or officer is individually a non-resident, enter the individual's foreign tax identification number and attach a certificate of residence if treaty relief is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliations of gross revenue: colocation rack-space leasing, power and cooling surcharges, bare-metal server hosting, maintenance contracts, cross-border bandwidth, and equipment procurement margin.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide income because the Chusik Hoesa is a Korean domestic corporation. Segregate Korean-source from foreign-source revenue and, in the international-transaction schedule, identify revenue arising from transactions with non-resident affiliates. All ACH and SWIFT wire settlements must be traceable to contracts, invoices, and bank statements; any revenue parked in foreign accounts must be added back unless genuinely attributable to a foreign permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and deductible items: book-to-tax reconciliation of non-deductible entertainment expenses, related-party interest exceeding thin capitalization limits, income from foreign subsidiaries, tax depreciation, provisions, and expenses not evidenced by tax invoices.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: In an audit against a non-resident parent, expenses must satisfy arm's length standards and economic reality. Deny promoters' overhead recharges unless supported by a transfer pricing study; deny power costs invoiced by a related party if the related party did not provide the power; and quarantine costs arising from a foreign head office unless a valid cost contribution arrangement and Local File exist.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of tax base: gross taxable income less deductible expenditures, applicable losses carried forward, and tax exemption amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the statutory loss-carryforward limit of 5 years for Korean corporate purposes unless a special statutory extension applies. Non-resident owners should ensure that losses are not restructured by intercompany transactions to shift profits; transfer pricing adjustments under Article 5 of LCITA may be proposed if losses arise from below-cost off-market contracts with affiliates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax rate schedule and calculation: progressive national corporate tax rates, alternative minimum tax, and local income tax surtax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate national corporate tax on the final tax base after adjustments; then compute local surtax at 10% of the national tax. For non-resident shareholders claiming an effective foreign tax credit, credit is limited to the Korean pre-credit tax on foreign-source income that remains subject to Korean tax; a DTA with a foreign state cannot be applied unilaterally if Box 5 tax is reduced below zero.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, tax reductions, foreign tax credit, and the withholding tax set-off for taxes withheld at source on corporate income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Schedule 16 and calculate foreign tax credits in strict order: (1) domestic credits; (2) treaty foreign tax credit; (3) unilateral foreign tax credit. If the corporation has received Korean-source dividends, interest, or royalties from a non-resident payer, reconcile tax withheld under the Korean Income Tax Act and take the credit against final corporate tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident payments and withholding declarations: outbound dividends declared, interest paid to non-resident lenders, royalties paid for software licensing, and fees for technical services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report, in separate schedules, each non-resident payee, the gross amount, the statutory WHT of 22% (20% non-resident tax plus 2% local surtax), and any treaty-reduced rate. Claims for DTA relief require the non-resident beneficial owner's Tax Residency Certificate, full beneficial-ownership documentation, an application to treaty application prior to remittance, and proof that the Chusik Hoesa is the withholding agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance due or refund: aggregate tax, less prepayments, estimated tax payments, and withheld amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any underpayment of WHT on outbound remittances not collected at source remains the personal liability of the directors and withholding agent. Electronic filing must be finalized before the deadline; a refund claim must be evidenced by actual wire details and tax invoices. A balance due in excess of KRW 10 million may be subject to additional tax if not paid within the statutory installment period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: non-declaration surtax equal to 20% of the unpaid tax under Framework Act on National Taxes (FANT) Article 47-2, plus monthly interest and daily delay surcharge for each day overdue, currently calculated at an annual rate of 10.95% on the unpaid amount. Underreporting: 10% of the omitted tax for negligent omission and 40% for fraudulent intent under FANT Article 47-3; a false or excessive refund claim triggers Article 47-5 penalties. Failure to file or maintain transfer pricing documentation is penalized by a formal fine and adverse evidentiary inferences; intentional evasion is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, exposing directors to imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine of up to 5 times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% statutory aggregate: 20% Korean non-resident corporate income tax withheld under the Income Tax Act, plus a 10% local surtax (2 percentage points), bringing the gross statutory WHT to 22%. Most Korean bilateral tax treaties reduce this rate to 5-15% for portfolio or substantial-holding dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Korean payer and withholding agent must invoke the DTA at source before remittance. Procedure: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) for the non-resident shareholder issued by the foreign tax authority, dated within the tax year; (2) submit the Application for Exemption from or Reduction of Withholding Tax under Tax Convention through HomeTax with supporting schedules; (3) prove beneficial ownership: the recipient must not be a conduit, must show capacity to benefit, own the shares for a meaningful period, and exercise economic substance, supported by board resolution, share register, audited financial statements, contract, and payment invoice; (4) provide evidence that no main-purpose or treaty-by-pass motive exists under the OECD BEPS-prevention clause; (5) instruct the bank to apply the treaty rate only after NTS acceptance or a documented treaty claim position. If treaty relief is denied or payment was made at statutory 22%, the recipient may file a refund claim with the district tax office having jurisdiction within 3 years; a complete protective claim requires TRC, evidence of gross-basis withholding, and a statement that the applicant is the beneficial owner.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory domestic WHT on royalties and interest paid to non-residents is also 22% aggregate (20% plus 2% local surtax). Under Korea's network of DTA protocols, interest and royalties are frequently reduced to 0%-15% (for instance 10% under many treaties; 0% for genuine bank interest in some peers; royalties for industrial or technical know-how often 10% or 15%). If a data-center colocation contract bundles lease, power, connectivity, and software, the fee must be broken down: pure rack-space lease is business income attributable to a Korean PE; technology royalty elements remain royalty withholding; failure to unbundle may attract a gross-up.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5 billion or more of aggregate related-party cross-border transactions in the taxable year triggers mandatory Local File and related-party transaction schedules; consolidated revenue of KRW 100 billion with cross-border intercompany transactions of KRW 5 billion or more triggers the Master File. A combined report and TP documentation must be submitted within 45 days of NTS request; failure creates a presumption in favor of the tax authority's arm's length adjustment under Article 5-6 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea applies the economic-substance doctrine through FANT Article 14, the substance-over-form principle in corporate taxation, and LCITA's international tax adjustment and CFC rules. For a data-center colocation lessor, the core income-generating activities (CIGA) are: acquiring and leasing the data-center site, owning and maintaining servers and rack hardware, employing technical engineers to manage power, cooling, and network uptime, negotiating and signing customer agreements, and bearing residual operating and currency risk. Treaty and reduced-rate benefits are denied if those CIGA are performed by a foreign subsidiary while the Korean entity is reduced to a pass-through contract manufacturer with no local people, assets, or functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation Under Korean LCITA and Corporate Tax Law
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Chusik Hoesa leases server racks and provides managed hosting to a Singapore or Hong Kong sales affiliate at a contract margin below cost, while the foreign affiliate books the true revenue and retains 85% of the consolidated profit. No Local File is prepared despite cross-border intercompany revenue exceeding the statutory threshold, and the NTS makes a downward arm's length adjustment of the Korean entity's income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Korean tax law permits the tax authority to disregard the contractual price and impose an arm's length adjustment under Articles 4 and 5 of the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs. The underassessed tax attracts an underreporting additional tax of 40% under FANT Article 47-3, daily late-payment interest on the shortfall, and a formal penalty for deliberate failure to submit TP documentation. The director who signed the non-arm's length contracts may be cited in the criminal referral.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil piercing: Korean courts will treat the corporate entity as a sham if it exists solely to evade tax, allowing creditors and the NTS to attach the directors' personal bank accounts, Seoul real estate, and shares. The CEO and CFO are jointly and severally liable to the company and to third parties under Commercial Act Article 401 for intentional or negligent mismanagement; criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act carries up to 5 years' imprisonment and a fine up to 5 times the tax evaded for the dominant director.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse of the Korean-Foreign DTA and Beneficial Ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Newly formed Chusik Hoesa is owned 99% by a Luxembourg shell controlled by a non-treaty beneficial owner; the Korean company pays dividends and a large 15% royalty for server software each year to the shell, which has no employees, no CIGA, no investment risk, and merely forwards funds onward. The DTA claim for a 5% reduced withholding is filed without a genuine beneficial-ownership certificate or a substantive foreign office.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS denies the treaty claim and imposes 22% domestic WHT, plus 10% local surcharge, plus underreporting additional tax of 40%, and a criminal referral for willful tax evasion. The distributing corporation remains liable as the withholding agent; non-collection is a serious criminal default. The Luxembourg shell is struck from treaty protection under the OECD Limitation-on-Benefits intention standard read through Korean DTA protocols.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Korean representative director is personally liable for the full un-withheld tax, additional tax, and local surcharge because the corporation was used as a conduit and the director knowingly signed the false treaty application. The NTS blacklists the director; the court may impose a Korean entry or travel ban for repeat tax offenders. Civil liability extends to restitution from the director's own assets where corporate funds were drained by the non-resident vendor and the Korean company is insolvent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Criminal False Tax Return and Obstruction of a Tax Audit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The company omits ACH and SWIFT wire revenue from ten overseas colocation clients, understates rack occupancy, claims fictitious power and repair expenses through a related non-resident vendor, and instructs the accountants to file a false corporate income tax return. The directors then provide fabricated data-center uptime logs and fake invoices during an NTS audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The criminal false-return charge is punishable under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act Article 3 by imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine of up to 5 times the evaded tax, and both imprisonment and fine may be imposed cumulatively. The NTS imposes 40% fraudulent underreporting penalties plus daily late payment surcharges; the tax return is reopened for prior years and tax positions in all years are collapsed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil piercing: directors who devised the false invoices and wire-omission scheme are stripped of limited liability and are personally liable for the evaded tax principal and penalties, including the daily surcharge for the entire period of concealment. The CFO and CEO face actual criminal imprisonment; the NTS liens on their houses and bank accounts, freezes inbound and outbound funds, alerts Korean Customs to exit-control and travel-ban, and disqualifies the convicted director from acting as an officer of any Korean company for 10 years.
